title: Concurrent Kernel Rendezvous — Weekly Report
summary: Notes and decisions from this week's kernel + KV cache + batching sync. Focus on rendezvous protocol changes, concurrent batch shaping, and shadow-kv experiments. Includes observed regression with short-sequence traffic and provisional mitigations.
content:
Week: 2029-12-02 -> 2029-12-04
Attendees: Maya, Diego, Priya, Samir, Lina, ops-oncall (evening shift)
Channel: #serving-runtime-kernel (thread: concurrent-rendezvous-2029-12)

1) Quick context / goal
- Goal this week: stabilize concurrent rendezvous handshake (handshake_v2) and validate that KV shadowing v3 doesn't introduce tail latency spikes under production mixed-traffic.
- Hypothesis: allowing concurrent kernel rendezvous (multiple kernels negotiating batches simultaneously) increases GPU utilization by ~8–12% for mixed short/long sequences while keeping p95 latency within SLO if we clamp coalescing window to 4–6ms.

2) What we changed / tried
- Deployed handshake_v2 (non-blocking rendezvous) to staging (canary slice: 3% traffic) on Dec 2 03:10 UTC. Config: rendezvous.max_concurrent=4, rendezvous.backoff_ms=2.
- Enabled kv-shadowing v3 (prefetch-backpressure tuned) on the same canary. Shadowing writes only; read path still hits stable cache.
- Introduced a new batch-split heuristic experiment: "time-first" (window-based) vs "size-first" (token-count threshold). A/B routed by request hash.
- Temporary metric added: kernel_handoff_wait_ms (captures time between kernel ready and accepted batch).

3) Observations (staging canary)
- Positive: GPU occupancy up ~9% during peak injects (12:00–13:00 UTC synthetic spike). CPU scheduling overhead did not increase materially.
- Regression: p99 latency for short sequences (avg len < 12 tokens) spiked by ~45% when kv-shadowing v3 and handshake_v2 were both enabled. Root cause suspected: short sequences are being coalesced into multi-kernel handoffs due to rendezvous concurrency, then delayed by prefill backpressure when KV prefetch queue is busy.
- Batch composition: time-first heuristic created a higher variance of batch sizes (3–60 tokens) compared to size-first which stayed tighter (4–18 tokens) under similar arrival patterns.

4) Root-cause analysis notes
- Timeline: short requests arrive -> rendezvous accepts multiple kernels -> batching waits up to rendezvous.window_ms -> kv-prefill starts but queue hits soft-limit due to concurrent prefetch tasks -> prefetch throttler delays some kernels -> kernel_handoff_wait_ms increases -> short sequences get held longer than intended.
- Data: captured 2400 traces of short-seq requests during the canary window. Median extra wait: 3.8ms, p95 extra wait: 9.4ms. Prefetch queue depth peaked at 128 (soft limit 100).
- Hypothesis validated by toggling kv-shadowing off while leaving handshake_v2 on: p99 returns near baseline.

5) Decisions made in sync
- Revert kv-shadowing v3 write-side prefetching on canary while keeping handshake_v2 enabled for further kernel-only experiments. Rationale: reduce variable backpressure while we test rendezvous concurrency benefits. Action: Diego to flip shadowing flag (done 2029-12-03 02:25 UTC).
- Short-term mitigation: clamp rendezvous.window_ms to max 5ms for requests flagged as short-sequence (heuristic: estimated_tokens <= 16). Implemented as a route-level override.
- Continue time-first vs size-first A/B but lower traffic to 1% each to collect cleaner signals.

6) Experiment plan next week
- Objective: quantify tradeoffs (throughput, p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization) for rendezvous concurrency levels [1,2,4] with kv-shadowing off, and then reintroduce controlled prefetch with a stricter prefetch-cap (50).
- Metrics to capture: kernel_handoff_wait_ms, prefetch_queue_depth, batch_size_distribution, GPU_util, p50/p95/p99 latency per seq-length bucket.
- Add a synthetic workload that mirrors production short/long mix (70% short < 16 tokens, 30% long > 128 tokens) to stress test queue interactions.

7) Operational notes / playbook updates
- Oncall checklist updated: if p99_short_seq > 2x baseline, steps: (1) set rendezvous.max_concurrent=1; (2) set rendezvous.window_ms=2ms; (3) disable kv-shadowing; (4) open incident; (5) capture 5k traces. Added to runbook (PR: #4123).
- Added alert: prefetched_queue_depth > 110 for >10s -> paging to ops.

8) Outstanding bugs / followups
- INF-8792: prefetcher leak under heavy long-sequence load still reproducible in local stress harness. Priority: P1. Assigned: Priya.
- INF-8834: race condition when rendezvous.backoff_ms=0 that causes batch duplication in corner case. Priority: P2. Assigned: Samir.
- Monitoring gap: we need a per-kernel prefetch latency histogram (proposal: sample 1/100 requests). Owner: Lina.

9) Action items (owner — ETA)
- Diego: revert kv-shadowing on canary (done 2029-12-03) — status: done.
- Priya: reproduce INF-8792 in CI harness and post a minimal repro (ETA 2029-12-06) — status: in_progress.
- Samir: add safe-guard in rendezvous code to avoid duplicate batches when backoff_ms==0 (PR draft) (ETA 2029-12-09) — status: in_progress.
- Lina: instrument per-kernel prefetch latency histogram and add dashboard panel (ETA 2029-12-11) — status: todo.
- Maya: run extended canary with rendezvous.max_concurrent in {1,2,4} and kv-shadowing off (ETA start 2029-12-05) — status: todo.

10) Meeting notes / decisions log
- 2029-12-02 17:00 UTC: handshake_v2 rolled to canary (3%).
- 2029-12-03 02:25 UTC: kv-shadowing v3 reverted on canary due to short-seq p99 regression.
- 2029-12-03 12:40 UTC: temporary clamp for short-request rendezvous.window_ms set to 5ms.
- All decisions captured in PR commentary and canary runbook.

11) Oddities / brainstorms (raw)
- Could we make prefetch adaptive per-request by predicting whether a request will be short/long earlier (tokenized size estimator at ingress)? Low-cost classifier might cut unnecessary prefetches.
- Consider small per-kernel prefetch quotas (e.g., 16 outstanding prefetches) to avoid global queue saturation from a few noisy kernels.
- Idea: route extremely short sequences to a fastpath kernel that never triggers KV prefetch; use this for high-volume micro-requests (search/QA autocomplete).

12) Next sync
- Weekly follow-up: 2029-12-09 16:00 UTC (agenda: replay canary metrics, deeper trace correlation, status on INF-8792 and prefetch histogram).

Appendix: quick numeric snapshot (staging canary, 2029-12-02 12:00 -> 2029-12-03 12:00 UTC)
- Requests sampled: 42,700
- Short-seq (<16 tokens) requests: 29,950 (70%)
- GPU util baseline: 64% -> with handshake_v2: 73% (peak)
- p50 short: 4.2ms -> 4.7ms (delta 0.5ms)
- p95 short: 9.8ms -> 12.3ms (delta 2.5ms)
- p99 short: 21.7ms -> 31.4ms (delta 9.7ms)
- Prefetch queue peak: 128 (soft limit 100)

Notes-to-self: keep canary windows small when toggling both kernel and cache features. Try to keep a single variable change per canary until prefetch behavior understood.
